Corticobasal degeneration is a chronic tauopathy, not acute basal-ganglia T2 hyperintensity.
MRS lactate peak can suggest lactic acidosis, but blood gas had no acidosis; it is a related metabolic finding, not EPS-CKDD.

Basal ganglia disease is an anatomic parent missing the CKD/dialysis extrapyramidal syndrome.
Multiple system atrophy is a neurodegenerative synucleinopathy, not this metabolic MRI pattern.
Diabetic amyotrophy is a lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy, not basal-ganglia parkinsonism.
Huntington disease is a chronic chorea syndrome, not acute dialysis basal-ganglia injury.
CJD has a different MRI/clinical course and does not produce lentiform fork sign.
Vitamin B1 was normal; Wernicke encephalopathy affects mammillary bodies/medial thalami.
Diabetic neuropathy is a peripheral process, not this central extrapyramidal syndrome.
Hypertensive encephalopathy/PRES has a different posterior-predominant pattern.
A lactate peak raises mitochondrial disease as a related differential, not EPS-CKDD.
Progressive supranuclear palsy is a neurodegenerative tauopathy, not acute dialysis basal-ganglia injury.
Metabolic disorder is a broad parent of dialysis-related basal ganglia injury.
